items.title: memoryGetCommunity: published export with zero callers, divergent inline live handler, sole test that cannot pass
items.status: open — root cause fully confirmed; fix surface requires a product ruling (delete-vs-align) that CHORE-MEMORY-001 already supplies direction on

evidence: (a) Zero-caller on main: CONFIRMED. The export `memoryGetCommunity` (libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:956-1039) is referenced ONLY by its own re-export (libs/memory-core/src/index.ts:279), the dead acceptance harness (tools/test-communities.js:19,144,156,165), and a dead plan doc (docs/plan/client-refactor/ARCH.md:74). No *.spec.ts anywhere references it; memory-server has its own inline handler and never imports the export. Grep across libs/, apps/, extensions/, tools/ finds no other caller.

(b) Divergence, export vs live handler (live handler is authoritative): the export (extensions.ts:956-1039) takes (adapter, entity_uid, level?) and returns {community:{uid,name,summary,level,member_count,members:[{uid,name,content,kind}]}} with members NESTED inside community, a `name` field, NO cluster_scope filter, and NO kind constraint on its node lookup (it resolves ANY live node kind — including entity nodes — via MEMBER_OF, i.e. it is the entity→community resolver). The live handler (extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:1702-1801) takes {entity_uid?, community_uid?, level?}, returns {community:{uid,label,member_count,mean_intra_sim,centroid_episode_uid,t_created}, members:[{uid,summary,topic,importance,t_created,project_path,tags}]} with members TOP-LEVEL, a `label` field, filters cluster_scope.kind='global', orders members by importance DESC, and accepts community_uid directly (the export cannot). Errors: export returns a plain {code:'E_NOT_FOUND',message} object; the live handler wraps in MCP isError. The live handler is authoritative: it is the shipped MCP surface documented in the server README/CLAUDE.md/extension.json (v1.1.0, breaking `name`→`label` change recorded). Divergence origin: commit 0ff4d812 (2026-07-02, 'consolidate memory-core, wire handleToolCall to core, delete client/') deleted the client/get-community.ts wrapper that consumed the export (per ARCH.md:74) and reimplemented the handler inline with v1 semantics, orphaning the export.

(c) Missing await in the sole test — BL-325 shape: tools/test-communities.js:144,156,165 call `memoryGetCommunity(db, uid, 0)` WITHOUT await; line 146 `assert(aliceCommunity.community !== undefined)` then FAILS on the Promise (and line 145 `!('code' in …)` passes vacuously — the false-negative pattern). Independently fatal: line 109 calls `buildCommunities(...)` without await (async per extensions.ts:766) so `buildResult.communities` is undefined and line 112 fails FIRST; lines 189/195/198 call `memorySearchEntities` without await (async per extensions.ts:1080) so line 190 fails too. Independently fatal #2: line 21 imports from '../extensions/mcp-servers/memory-server/dist/lib.js' — that path does not exist on main (`extensions/mcp-servers/` directory is absent; the server lives under extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server), so the test cannot even resolve its imports. The test cannot pass at any of three independent layers.

(d) Fix surface options: (1) align the live handler onto the export — WRONG direction: the export's contract is obsolete (name vs label, nested members, no mean_intra_sim, no community_uid arg, no cluster_scope filter); aligning would regress the shipped v1.1.0 surface. (2) delete the export — correct under CHORE-MEMORY-001 (see item 2): the export is the only code that actually performs the entity→community resolution being retired, and @adhd/sox-memory-core (v0.7.0) has zero external consumers (all consumers are workspace:* — memory-server, memory-flush, memory-cli, tools/baseline-capture), so deletion is practically risk-free but IS a semver-breaking change to the package's public API and needs a changeset with the breaking marker. (3) fix the test — pointless: the import path is dead and the contract under test is obsolete; the P4 acceptance role it served is now covered by memory-tools.spec.ts (skip-guarded C2.6 block at memory-tools.spec.ts:714) and, once merged, the unconditional bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts.

CHORE-MEMORY-001's owner ruling ('do NOT build entity→community resolution; the need is served by memory_entity_episodes; "the" community of an entity is not well-defined') bears directly: it answers (d) as DELETE, not align. The export exists only to serve the retired capability.
unverified: Claim 'PUBLISHED' from the issue: libs/memory-core/package.json has no `"private": true` and is versioned 0.7.0, so it is technically publishable; but no external/npm consumer exists (verified workspace-only consumers). Whether any previously-published 0.x tarball is consumed out-of-tree cannot be verified from this repo.

That memory-tools.spec.ts:714's C2.6 describe block is skip-guarded (per the branch spec file's header comment, lines 9-12) — the guard code itself was read at :719 ('No clusters formed with hash backend at this scale — skip gracefully') and confirms the BL-167 pattern, but I did not run the suite to see the skip fire.

files: tools/test-communities.js (delete, or repair import path + awaits if the P4 harness is deemed load-bearing — it is not: superseded by memory-tools.spec.ts and the in-flight bug-memory-006 spec)
libs/memory-core/package.json (version bump if policy requires — no 'private': true)
fixSurface.shape: DELETE the export and its types; dispose of the dead acceptance harness (or minimally repair it only if a stakeholder wants the P4 narrative preserved); relabel the remaining live tool documentation to episode-only semantics (see item 2). Do NOT touch the live handler's behavior — it is authoritative and already correct (and the in-flight branch improves its error taxonomy).

blockedBy: CHORE-MEMORY-001 product ruling (delete-vs-align is the ruling's subject; the ruling direction 'retire entity→community' selects DELETE)

feat/bug-memory-006-community-affordance merge (the branch relabels the live tool's entity_uid description to episode-only and adds AC4 — an unconditional conformance test asserting the 'entity' claim is dropped from the schema — which is the doc-side half of this item's retirement surface; merging it first lets this packet land as pure deletion with the conformance guard already in place)
dependencies.ordering: Ruling first (product) → branch merge (backend, item 3) → deletion packet (implement) → red→green verification (test). No ordering coupling with the clustering triage packets (BL-495/BUG-010): those touch cluster.ts/cluster-metrics.ts and do not overlap this file set.

executor.agent: product for the ruling; implement (pro tier) for the mechanical deletion; test for the red→green guard

testPlan.name: memory_get_community surface consolidation (BUG-MEMORY-007)
testPlan.assertion: After deletion: (1) `rg memoryGetCommunity libs apps extensions tools` returns zero hits on the merged tree (compile/lint gate — the export is gone); (2) the live handler remains fully covered by the unconditional bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts AC1-AC6 (merged from the branch), which asserts E_WRONG_ID_SPACE advisory-on-miss, E_NOT_FOUND for well-formed-absent, E_PENDING_CLUSTER for unclustered episodes, E_WRONG_KIND for entity/community uids — the full post-consolidation contract; (3) memory-tools.spec.ts's skip-guarded C2.6 block is either replaced by the unconditional spec or deleted (BL-167 pattern removal).
testPlan.whyCatches: It proves the deletion did not silently strand the capability (no dangling export), that the consolidated contract (episode-only resolution, distinguishable error codes) is enforced by unconditional assertions rather than the BL-167 skip-guard, and that the dead harness's claims — which could not run — are replaced by a test that does. BL-225-compliant: the red arm is the pre-deletion tree where the dead test fails at tools/test-communities.js:112/:146 and the skip-guarded C2.6 block provides no coverage.

packet.recommendation: COMBINE with CHORE-MEMORY-001 — same surface, one ruling. One packet: 'retire entity→community affordance' (export deletion + doc relabel + dead-harness disposition), sequenced after the branch merge. Do NOT split into a separate alignment-vs-delete code packet: the alignment option is foreclosed by the ruling, so there is no independent decision left.
packet.scope: libs/memory-core (extensions.ts, index.ts, package.json/changeset), memory-server docs (extension.json:122, README.md:35), tools/test-communities.js
packet.risk: LOW. Zero production callers; all consumers workspace-local; the live handler is untouched. Only risk: forgetting the semver-breaking changeset for the published (but unconsumed) @adhd/sox-memory-core API, and accidentally deleting the load-bearing episode→community resolution while removing entity→community — the packet must distinguish the two (the branch's E_WRONG_KIND narrowing is the marker that the live path is episode-only and stays).

items.title: Retire the advertised entity→community capability (product ruling: 'the' community of an entity is not well-defined; need served by memory_entity_episodes)
items.status: open — ruling direction confirmed; concrete retirement surface enumerated; minimal surface is small and partially already in flight on the branch

evidence: What 'retire the advertised capability' concretely means, by surface, on main HEAD 3e9a40c0:

1. DEAD code that performs entity→community: `memoryGetCommunity` (extensions.ts:956-1039) — its node lookup (line 963-972) has NO kind constraint, so it resolves any live node (including kind='entity') through MEMBER_OF to a community. Zero callers (item 1). This is the only remaining implementation of the retired capability.

2. ADVERTISED doc claims to retire/relabel: extension.json:122 tool description 'Get community node for an entity.'; README.md:35 'Look up the community cluster for an entity or community node'; extensions.ts:952-953 doc comment 'Returns the community a node belongs to' (any-node implication); index.ts:267 section comment 'Extended functions (promotion, graphify, communities, entity search)'; tools/test-communities.js:7 assertion header '(b) memoryGetCommunity(entity_uid) → resolves entity to its community' (broken harness, item 1).

3. LOAD-BEARING and KEPT (episode→community, NOT entity→community): the live handler's entity_uid path (index.ts:1702-1801) — on main its TOOLS description still says 'episode/entity UID' (index.ts:502), but the in-flight branch narrows it to kind='episode' (E_WRONG_KIND for entity/community/session uids) and relabels the schema description to drop 'entity'. That narrowing IS the retirement's code-side half and is already authored on the branch.
4. Replacement already live: `memory_entity_episodes` (entity-episodes.ts, re-exported index.ts:327) returns episodes mentioning an entity — the ruling's designated replacement.

Minimal retirement surface: delete export + types + re-exports (item 1 file set); rewrite extension.json:122 and README.md:35 to describe episode→community lookup; merge the branch's entity_uid narrowing + AC4 conformance test; delete or repair tools/test-communities.js. The live handler itself is untouched.

Note: the live tool's `entity_uid` PARAMETER NAME is load-bearing API (documented, schema-exposed, MCP callers pass it); retiring the capability does not mean renaming the parameter — it means the parameter's documented scope narrows to episodes and kind='entity' inputs get E_WRONG_KIND instead of a community.
unverified: Whether any out-of-tree consumer reads the extension.json:122 'for an entity' wording as a promise (host configs are generated from extension.json but the description is informational — cannot verify external expectation)
The exact line numbers of README.md:35 and extension.json:122 on the post-merge tree if the branch's description changes collide — they do not overlap, but I verified against main HEAD only

files: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:495-517 (TOOLS schema — already authored on the branch: entity_uid description drops 'entity', names E_PENDING_CLUSTER)
tools/test-communities.js (delete, or repair if the P4 narrative is wanted)
functions: handleToolCall memory_get_community entity_uid path (narrow to kind='episode' — on branch)
fixSurface.shape: One deletion + four doc relabels + the branch's already-authored narrowing. The retirement is a documentation-and-dead-code operation; no live behavior changes beyond what the branch already authored.

blocks: BUG-MEMORY-007's (d) fix-surface choice (its delete-vs-align question is answered here: delete)
blockedBy: feat/bug-memory-006-community-affordance merge — its AC4 test (bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts:240-251) asserts the 'entity' claim is dropped from the tool schema and the E_WRONG_KIND narrowing is implemented; this packet completes the retirement around that already-authored core
dependencies.ordering: Branch merge first (backend), then this packet (product ruling → implement deletion → test verification). Same ordering as item 1 — they are the same packet.

executor.agent: product (confirms retirement scope and the parameter-name-kept decision), implement (pro) for deletion/relabel, test for the doc-conformance red→green

testPlan.name: entity→community retirement conformance (CHORE-MEMORY-001)
testPlan.assertion: (1) The branch's AC4 test passes: TOOLS[memory_get_community] description and entity_uid property description no longer match /entity/i, community_uid description still mentions 'global and subset'. (2) A new/merged regression asserts kind='entity' entity_uid returns {code:'E_WRONG_KIND', kind:'entity'} and no community (branch's AC6 test, spec:283-311). (3) Post-deletion `rg -l 'GetCommunity|memoryGetCommunity'` over src/ is empty. (4) extension.json:122 and README.md:35 no longer contain 'entity' in the get_community description (doc-conformance assertion — could live in the server's spec suite reading extension.json).
testPlan.whyCatches: Each arm pins a distinct surface of the retirement: the schema advertisement (AC4), the runtime behavior for entity inputs (AC6), the dead-code removal (grep gate), and the extension-manifest advertisement (doc assertion). Together they prevent the exact failure mode the ruling exists for — an 'entity→community' claim surviving anywhere in the advertised surface while the implementation is gone, or vice versa.

packet.recommendation: COMBINE with BUG-MEMORY-007 into one 'retire entity→community affordance' packet (same surface, one product ruling, one deletion, one doc relabel). The packet ships after the branch merges so AC4/AC6 are the conformance guard it rides on.
packet.scope: libs/memory-core export surface + memory-server manifest/README + tools/test-communities.js + changeset
packet.risk: LOW-MEDIUM. LOW: pure deletion + relabel, live behavior untouched, zero callers. MEDIUM dimension: the relabel touches the ADVERTISED tool description that MCP clients see in tools/list — an external agent could be relying on the 'entity' wording; that is precisely the advertised-capability the ruling retires, so the risk is intentional and the AC4 test makes it visible, not silent.

items.title: Merge-readiness assessment of the in-flight branch (both prior review findings reported closed at bed42917)
items.status: assessed — both closures verified REAL; merge mechanically clean; recommend fast re-review then merge (not parked)

evidence: Closure 1 (community_uid pre-query hard-reject) — VERIFIED on the diff. At bed42917 the `if (communityUidArg)` branch is reduced to `commUid = communityUidArg;` with an explanatory comment; the 32-hex/ULID shape test (COMMUNITY_UID_RE/ULID_RE) was MOVED from the pre-query hard-reject (git show bed42917 removes it from the top of the branch) into the `!commRow` miss path (index.ts:1773-1798 on the branch) where it fires as advisory E_WRONG_ID_SPACE only after the lookup missed. A legacy-shaped community uid that resolves now succeeds. Regression test: bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts:111-152 (absent-but-32-hex → E_NOT_FOUND, not E_WRONG_ID_SPACE; direct-adapter-written legacy-shaped community node resolves successfully). Commit message records red→green watched per BL-225.

Closure 2 (SPEC-BUG-MEMORY-006.md §1b/D2/D4) — VERIFIED on the diff. §1b heading now reads '…but the format is NOT the only minting scheme, so a shape check can only ever be advisory' (SPEC-BUG-MEMORY-006.md:56); body names buildCommunities (extensions.ts:843) as the second minting site (line 74-83); D2/D4 rulings revised to 'advisory-only, not a hard reject' (lines 336-368). The false 'only site that ever writes a kind=community uid' claim is gone.

Merge mechanics — CLEAN. `git merge-tree --write-tree --messages main HEAD` (branch worktree) → exit 0, tree 1bd58c73, single 'Auto-merging extensions/.../memory-server/src/index.ts'. The branch's hunks (TOOLS schema L490-517, handler L1695-1800) do not overlap main's 5 hunks since merge-base 214a91b9 (L46 imports, L988, L1086, L2362, L2391) — semantically safe, not just mechanically clean. PLAN.md/STATE.md changed on both sides but with the SAME derived-count refresh (BL-495/496/497 added by main's a068ef0e and the branch's 8c2c96a1); the merged tree contains the branch's line and carries no conflict markers.

API compatibility of the branch's tests against main's newer libs: clusterStore(db,{threshold}) still exported from main's cluster.ts:993 with threshold?: number in ClusterStoreOptions (cluster.ts:94); memory_write still returns episode_uid; memory_search_entities still returns entities[].uid — all assertions in the branch spec hold against main's current API.

Branch changeset (main...HEAD): 5 files only — SPEC-BUG-MEMORY-006.md (new), PLAN.md/STATE.md (derived refresh), bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts (new, 312 lines), memory-server/src/index.ts (84 lines). Zero overlap with the clustering triage packets' files (cluster.ts, cluster-metrics.ts, enrich.ts, stages.ts, write.ts are untouched by the branch).

Regression test quality: HIGH. Real MCP seam (drives handleToolCall directly), unconditional assertions, deterministic fixtures (explicit clusterStore passes, deliberate omission for E_PENDING_CLUSTER), explicitly avoids the BL-167 skip-guard pattern (header lines 9-15), covers AC1-AC6 including both review-finding regressions.
unverified: Test-green claim (memory-server 34 files / 240 tests) is self-reported in the session-state doc and commit message — I am read-only triage and did not run the suite; session state also flags the harness returned 'mergeable: true' for this wave while the reviewer's prose said NOT MERGEABLE (tooling defect).

Smoke test and registry sync-index have not been run on the branch (required by AGENTS.md before merging any MCP-server extension change) — no build/dist was produced on the branch, so registry checksums are unaffected, but the smoke gate must still be run at merge time.
No changeset file exists on the branch (main's convention: .changeset/bug-memory-001-*.md, .changeset/conn-recycle-*.md for memory-server fixes).

files: No code changes demanded by this assessment. Merge-time additions only: .changeset/bug-memory-006-community-affordance.md (new), post-merge `tools/plan-status.mjs --check` (PLAN/STATE drift), smoke test run.
fixSurface.shape: Merge as-is after: (1) one fast re-review of the two closures (reviewer that ruled NOT MERGEABLE never re-reviewed), (2) adding the changeset, (3) running the suite + smoke gate. Optional cosmetic: stale comment line-ref 'index.ts:1706-1712' in bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts:85 (the guard moved to the miss path) — update to the new location.

blocks: BUG-MEMORY-007 / CHORE-MEMORY-001 packets (they ride on this branch's AC4/AC6 conformance tests and entity_uid narrowing)
dependencies.ordering: Independent of BL-495/BUG-010 and the clustering triage packets — the branch touches no cluster-pipeline file. The session-state ordering note ('BL-496 merges first, guard rebases on top') applies to feat/cluster-tracing, NOT this branch. E_PENDING_CLUSTER is the diagnosable complement to BUG-MEMORY-010's visibility gap (it names the not-yet-clustered state instead of lying with E_NOT_FOUND), an interaction, not a dependency. Merge now, ahead of the clustering wave if scheduling allows; at minimum not blocked by it.

executor.agent: backend (merge owner — authored by backend-developer per commit citations); review (fast re-review of the two closures)

testPlan.name: Branch suite + post-merge gates (feat/bug-memory-006-community-affordance)
testPlan.assertion: npx nx test memory-server --skip-nx-cache (with check-suite-tree-state.mjs tree-state quoted) shows 34 files green including the 10 new bug-memory-006 tests; typecheck + lint clean; `node tools/plan-status.mjs --check` passes post-merge; smoke test 0 failures per AGENTS.md (MCP-server extension changed).
testPlan.whyCatches: The BL-456 lesson: a suite result is evidence only with the tree state stated; the 240-green claim is currently unattributable to me. The unconditional (non-skip-guarded) assertions are what make the new spec a real gate rather than a BL-167 shadow.

packet.recommendation: MERGE NOW after a fast re-review of the two closures + changeset + suite/smoke gates — do NOT park behind BL-495/BUG-010 (zero file overlap, no semantic ordering dependency). If review bandwidth is zero, the closures are verifiable from the diff and the regression tests are BL-225-shaped, so a merge-then-post-review is defensible but not preferred (the tool-surface change adds new error codes E_WRONG_KIND/E_PENDING_CLUSTER to a live MCP tool — that's API surface worth one reviewer's pass).
packet.scope: memory-server tool surface (memory_get_community description + error taxonomy) + SPEC-BUG-MEMORY-006.md + regression spec
packet.risk: LOW-MEDIUM. LOW: clean merge, strong tests, no cluster-pipeline touch. MEDIUM: new error codes are API additions to a live tool (clients switching on exact codes see new branches — but the codes only REPLACE a bare E_NOT_FOUND on paths that previously mislabeled, so strictly more informative); the 240-green claim is unverified by a second party; harness bug from the session ('mergeable: true' with NOT MERGEABLE prose) means the merge gate itself was unreliable.

inFlightBranchAssessment.evidence: Both review findings closed at bed42917 verified REAL on the diff: (1) community_uid shape check moved from pre-query hard-reject to the !commRow miss path as advisory E_WRONG_ID_SPACE — `git show bed42917` shows the removal of the pre-query block and its reappearance inside the not-found branch; regression tests at bug-memory-006-community-affordance.spec.ts:111-152 pin absent-32-hex→E_NOT_FOUND and legacy-shaped-resolving→success. inFlightBranchAssessment.recommendation: Merge after: one fast re-review of the two closures + add .changeset/bug-memory-006-community-affordance.md + run nx test/typecheck/lint + plan-status --check + smoke gate. Land it before the BUG-MEMORY-007/CHORE-MEMORY-001 retirement packet, which rides on its AC4/AC6 conformance tests.

openQuestions: BUG-MEMORY-007 (d): confirm the product ruling is DELETE (not align/fix-test) — CHORE-MEMORY-001's direction implies it, but the ruling should be recorded explicitly with the parameter-name-kept decision (entity_uid parameter name stays; only its documented scope narrows to episodes).

tools/test-communities.js: delete outright, or repair (fix import path + all awaits) to preserve the P4 acceptance narrative? Recommendation: delete — superseded by memory-tools.spec.ts + the branch spec; it has never run green (dead import path since the bundle move).

Does @adhd/sox-memory-core need a version bump + breaking changeset for the export deletion even though all consumers are workspace:*? Convention says yes (semver hygiene); external-consumer risk is nil (verified).

Merge mode for the branch: rebase onto main (37 commits of drift, clean per merge-tree) or merge-commit from the worktree? Merge-tree proves conflict-free either way; rebase keeps history linear and matches the session's pattern for the other in-flight branches.

Should the harness 'mergeable: true vs NOT MERGEABLE prose' tooling defect (session-state 'Tooling defect, unfiled') be filed? It silently mis-gated a merge decision — filing prevents recurrence. Out of scope for this report's packets but adjacent.
